questions.question: 36 persons can do a work in 10 days, working 6 hours a day. In how many days will 24 persons, working 9 hours a day complete the work?
questions.questionHtml: 36 persons can do a work in 10 days, working 6 hours a day. In how many days will 24 persons, working 9 hours a day complete the work?
questions.solution:
Given:

36 persons can do a work in 10 days, working 6 hours a day.

24 persons, working 9 hours a day.

Formula used:

Work = Number of persons × Number of days × Number of hours per day

Calculation:

Total work by 36 persons:

Work = 36 × 10 × 6

⇒ Work = 2160 hours

Now, let the number of days required by 24 persons be D:

Work = 24 × D × 9

⇒ 2160 = 24 × D × 9

⇒ D = 2160 / (24 × 9)

⇒ D = 10

∴ The correct answer is option 1.

questions.question: A can complete a piece of work in 9 days. B and C can complete the same work in 12 days and 18 days respectively. If A, B, C work together, then in how many days will they complete the work?
questions.questionHtml: A can complete a piece of work in 9 days. B and C can complete the same work in 12 days and 18 days respectively. If A, B, C work together, then in how many days will they complete the work?
questions.solution:
LCM of (9,12 and 18) = Total work done = 36

Efficiency of A = 36/9 = 4

Efficiency of B = 36/12 = 3

Efficiency of A = 36/18 = 2

Together, work will be done in = 36/(4 + 3 + 2) = 4 days.

questions.question: Vipin can do a piece of work in 2 days; Vaibhav can do the same work in 3 days and Chirag can do the same work in 6 days. If they start working together, how many days will they take to complete the work?
questions.questionHtml: Vipin can do a piece of work in 2 days; Vaibhav can do the same work in 3 days and Chirag can do the same work in 6 days. If they start working together, how many days will they take to complete the work?
questions.solution:
⇒ Total work = LCM of 2 ,3 and 6 = 6

⇒ vipin = 6/2 = 3, ⇒ vaibhav = 6/3 = 2, ⇒ chirag = 6/6 = 1

⇒Total work efficiency = 3 + 2 + 1 = 6

⇒ Work done together = 6 / 6 = 1 day.

questions.question: A and B can do a piece of work in 36 days. B and C can do the same work in 60 days. A and C can do the same work in 45 days. In how many days can A alone complete the same work?
questions.questionHtml: A and B can do a piece of work in 36 days. B and C can do the same work in 60 days. A and C can do the same work in 45 days. In how many days can A alone complete the same work?
questions.solution:
Given:

A and B can do a piece of work in 36 days

B and C can do the same work in 60 days

A and C can do the same work in 45 days

Concept used:

Total days of work = Work/(One day work)

Calculation:

1 day work of (A + B) = 1/36           …………..(1)

1 day work of (B + C) = 1/60           …………..(2)

1 day work of (A + C) = 1/45           …………..(3)

Adding (1), (2), and (3)

1 day work of 2(A + B + C) = 1/36 + 1/60 + 1/45

⇒ 1/36 + 1/60 + 1/45

⇒ (5 + 3 + 4)/180

⇒ 12/180

⇒ 1/15

⇒ 1 day work of (A + B + C) = 1/30

1 day work of A = 1 day work of (A + B + C) – 1 day work of (B + C)

⇒ 1 day work of A = 1/30 – 1/60

⇒ (2 – 1)/60

⇒ 1/60

Total number of days completed by A = Work/(1 day work of A)

⇒ Total number of days completed by A = 1/(1/60)

⇒ Total number of days completed by A = 60 days

∴ Total number of days completed by A is 60 days.

questions.question: At a construction site, Raju can paint a wall in 36 hours, while Angad can do the same work in 18 hours. Sumit can paint the same wall in 24 hours. In how much time can they paint the wall if they all work together?
questions.questionHtml: At a construction site, Raju can paint a wall in 36 hours, while Angad can do the same work in 18 hours. Sumit can paint the same wall in 24 hours. In how much time can they paint the wall if they all work together?
questions.solution:
Let, m = time taken by all three.

⇒ (1/36) + (1/18) + (1/24) = 1/m ⇒ (2 + 4 + 3)/72 = 1/m ⇒ m = 72/9 = 8

If all 3 work together, they will take 8 hours to paint the wall.

questions.question: Work done by 8 men is completed in 10 days. The same work can be completed in 12 days when done by 10 women. How many days will it take to complete when 4 men and 4 women are employed to perform the same job?
questions.questionHtml: Work done by 8 men is completed in 10 days. The same work can be completed in 12 days when done by 10 women. How many days will it take to complete when 4 men and 4 women are employed to perform the same job?
questions.solution:
Given : 

Work done by 8 men is completed in 10 days.

Same work can be completed in 12 days when done by 10 women.

Formula Used : 

M1H1D1/W1 = M2H2D2/W2

Calculation : 

⇒ 8M × 10 = 10W × 12

⇒ 80M = 120W

⇒ M/W = 120/80 = 3/2

Total Work = 8 × 3 × 10 = 240

Now, 240 = (4M + 4W) × time

⇒ time = 240/(4 × 3 + 4 × 2)

⇒ time = 240/20 = 12 days

∴ The correct answer is 12 days.

questions.question: 4 men and 6 women can complete a work in 8 days, while 3 men and 7 women can complete it in 10 days. In how many days will 10 women complete it?
questions.questionHtml: 4 men and 6 women can complete a work in 8 days, while 3 men and 7 women can complete it in 10 days. In how many days will 10 women complete it?
questions.solution:
(4m + 6w) × 8 = (3m + 7w) × 10 ⇒ 16m + 24w = 15m + 35w ⇒ 16m - 15m = 35w - 24w ⇒ m = 11w ⇒ m/w = 11/1

⇒ Total work = (4 × 11 + 6) × 8 ⇒ Total work = 400 unit

⇒ Time taken by 10 woman = 400/10 = 40 days

questions.question: 30 men working 5 hours a day can do work in 18 days. In how many days will 20 men working 7 hours a day do the same work?
questions.questionHtml: <!-- x-tinymce/html -->30 men working 5 hours a day can do work in 18 days. In how many days will 20 men working 7 hours a day do the same work?
questions.solution:
30 × 5 × 18 = 2700 man-hours ⇒ 20 × 7 × x = 2700 ⇒ x = 2700 / 140

x = 192/7

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 10 days, while A and B together can complete it in \(2\frac{1}{2}\) days. How long will B alone take to complete the work?
questions.questionHtml: A can do a piece of work in 10 days, while A and B together can complete it in \(2\frac{1}{2}\) days. How long will B alone take to complete the work?
questions.solution:
According to the question, ⇒ \(\frac{1}{10}+\frac{1}{B}=\frac{2}{5}\) ⇒ \(\frac{1}{B}=\frac{2}{5}-\frac{1}{10}\) ⇒ \(\frac{1}{B}=\frac{4-1}{10}\) = \(\frac{3}{10}\)

B alone will take \(\frac{10}{3}\) days to complete the work.

questions.question: Ravi and Mohan together can complete a task in 3 days. Ravi alone can complete the same task in 7 days. How many days will Mohan alone take to complete the same task?
questions.questionHtml: Ravi and Mohan together can complete a task in 3 days. Ravi alone can complete the same task in 7 days. How many days will Mohan alone take to complete the same task?
questions.solution:
Given 

Ravi and Mohan can complete work = 3 days

Ravi alone complete the work = 7 days

Formula Used

Work = time × efficiency 

Calculation

⇒ LCM of (3, 7) = 21

⇒ Let the total work be 21

⇒ Efficiency of Ravi and Mohan together = 21/3 = 7

⇒ Efficiency of Ravi alone = 21/7 = 3

⇒ Efficiency of Mohan = 7 - 3 = 4 

⇒ Mohan takes time to complete the work alone = 21/4 = \(5\frac{1}{4}\) days

questions.question: A earns Rs. 40 per hour and works for 12 hours. B earns Rs. 60 per hour and works for 10 hours. Find the ratio of their per day wages.
questions.questionHtml: A earns Rs. 40 per hour and works for 12 hours. B earns Rs. 60 per hour and works for 10 hours. Find the ratio of their per day wages.
questions.solution:
Given∶ Earning rate of A = Rs. 40 per hour

Working hour of A = 12

Earning rate of B = Rs. 60 per hour

Working hour of B = 10

Calculation∶

One day earning of A = 40 × 12 = Rs. 480

One day earning of B = 60 × 10 = Rs. 600

∴ Ratio of one day earning of A and one day earning of B = 480/600 = 4 ∶ 5

questions.question: P and Q can do a piece of work in 14 days. Q and R together can do it in 21 days. If P is twice as good a workman as R, then in how many days Q alone can do the work?
questions.questionHtml: P and Q can do a piece of work in 14 days. Q and R together can do it in 21 days. If P is twice as good a workman as R, then in how many days Q alone can do the work?
questions.solution:
Let P, Q and R can do the work in x, y, and z days respectively. 

A/Q ⇒ \(\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{y}=\frac{1}{14}\)  ⇒ \(\frac{1}{y}+\frac{1}{z}=\frac{1}{21}\) ⇒ As per the condition given, \(\frac{1}{x}=\frac{2}{z}\)

Putting the value in (1), and subtracting (2) from (1), we get ⇒ \(\frac{2}{z}+\frac{1}{y}-\frac{1}{z}-\frac{1}{y}=\frac{1}{14}-\frac{1}{21}\) ⇒ \(\frac{1}{z}=\frac{3-2}{42}=\frac{1}{42}\) ⇒ z = 42 days

Putting the value of z in equation (2), we get ⇒ \(\frac{1}{y}=\frac{1}{21}-\frac{1}{42}\) ⇒ y = 42 days

questions.question: O, T and P can do a piece of work in 3, 4 and 6 hours respectively. If they are working together, then in how much time they will finish the work?
questions.questionHtml: O, T and P can do a piece of work in 3, 4 and 6 hours respectively. If they are working together, then in how much time they will finish the work?
questions.solution:
Work done by O in one hour = 1/3 × 12 = 4

Work done by T in one hour = 1/4 × 12 = 3

Work done by P in one hour = 1/6 × 12 = 2

Total work done in one hour = 4 + 3 + 2 = 9

Time taken to finish the work = 1/(Total work done in one hour)

= 12/9 = 4/3 = 1 + 1/3 = 1 hour and 20 minutes

questions.question: A tap can fill a tank in 4 hours. Another tap can fill the same tank in 6 hours. If both the taps are opened at the same time, then in how much time will the empty tank be filled completely?
questions.questionHtml: A tap can fill a tank in 4 hours. Another tap can fill the same tank in 6 hours. If both the taps are opened at the same time, then in how much time will the empty tank be filled completely?
questions.solution:
Given:

A tap can fill a tank in 4 hours. Another tap can fill the same tank in 6 hours.

Concept used:

Entire work = Work done hourly × Total time taken (In hours)

Calculation:

LCM (4,6) = 12

Let us consider the capacity of the tank as the LCM of 4 and 6.

So, the capacity of the tank = 12 Units

Hourly filled,

By Tap A = 12 ÷ 4 = 3 units

By Tap B = 12 ÷ 6 = 2 units

Time taken to completely fill the tank when both A & B are opened

⇒ 12 ÷ (3 + 2)

⇒ 2.4 hours = 2 hours 24 minutes

∴ If both the taps are opened at the same time, 2 hours 24 minutes will take the empty tank to be filled completely.

questions.question: 5 men and 8 women can complete a work in 12 days working together, while 3 men and 7 women together can complete the same work in 15 days. In how many days will 11 women complete the same work?
questions.questionHtml: 5 men and 8 women can complete a work in 12 days working together, while 3 men and 7 women together can complete the same work in 15 days. In how many days will 11 women complete the same work?
questions.solution:
(5M + 8W) × 12 = (3M + 7W) × 15 ⇒ 15M = 9W  ⇒ M/W = 3/5

Now, time taken to complete the work by 11 women 

⇒ {(5M + 8W) × 12} ÷ 11W ⇒ {(5 × 3 + 8 × 5) × 12} ÷ 55 ⇒ {55 × 12} ÷ 55 ⇒ 12 days

questions.questionHtml: 6 labourers can finish a work in 16 days. 10 labourers are available, but the work is to be finished by 8 days. How many more labourers are to be called to finish the work in time?

Let the number of labour required be a.

⇒ (10 + a) × 8  = 96 ⇒ (10 + a) = 12 ⇒ a  = 2

questions.question: If 6 women can complete a work in 3 days, and 9 girls can complete the same work in 2 days, then find the time taken to complete the same work by 8 women and 6 girls?
questions.questionHtml: If 6 women can complete a work in 3 days, and 9 girls can complete the same work in 2 days, then find the time taken to complete the same work by 8 women and 6 girls?
questions.solution:
6W × 3 = 9G × 2 ⇒ W : G = 1 : 1

Total work = 6W × 3 = 6 × 3 = 18

Time taken to complete the same work by 8 women and 6 girls,

⇒ 18/(8W + 6G) ⇒ 18/(8 + 6) ⇒ 18/14 ⇒ 9/7

questions.question: A and B can complete a piece of work in 12 days. B and C can complete the same work in 15 days and C and A in 10 days. How many days will A take to complete the work by himself?
questions.questionHtml: A and B can complete a piece of work in 12 days. B and C can complete the same work in 15 days and C and A in 10 days. How many days will A take to complete the work by himself?
questions.solution:
a + b = 1/12, b + c = 1/15, c + a = 1/10

2(a + b + c) = 1/12 + 1/15 + 1/10 ⇒ 2(a + b + c) = (5/60) + (4/60) + (6/60)

2(a + b + c) = 15/60 = 1/4, a + b + c = 1/8

a + b = 1/12, 1/8 - c = 1/12, c = 1/24 ⇒ c + a = 1/10, a = 1/10 - 1/24

a = (12/120) - (5/120) = 7/120 ⇒ A's time = 120/7= \(17 \frac{1}{7}\)days.

questions.questionHtml: A can do a piece of work in 24 days and B can do the same work in 30 days. If they work on it together for 8 days, then the fraction of the work that is left is:
questions.solution:
Let total work is 120 units ( Lcm of 24 and 30)

Total Efficiency,  5 + 4 = 9 unit

Total work done in 8 days, 9 × 8 = 72 units

questions.question: Mahesh and Suresh can complete a work in 16 days and 12 days, respectively. Starting with Mahesh, they work on alternate basis. How many days will take to finalise the complete work?
questions.questionHtml: Mahesh and Suresh can complete a work in 16 days and 12 days, respectively. Starting with Mahesh, they work on alternate basis. How many days will take to finalise the complete work?
questions.solution:
Given:

Mahesh can complete the work in 16 days

Suresh can complete the work in 12 days

They work on the alternative basis

Formula Used:

Total work = Time taken x Efficiency

Calculations:

⇒ Total work = LCM of 16 and 12 = 48 

⇒ Efficiency of Mahesh = Total work / Time taken = 48 / 16 = 3

⇒ Efficiency of Suresh = Total work / Time taken = 48 / 12 = 4

⇒ The total efficiency of both = 7 

We can say that,

⇒ In 2 days = 7 work is completed

⇒ 12 days = 42 work

For 13 days Mahesh has to work 

⇒ 13 days = 42 + 3 = 45 work

The remaining work has to complete by Suresh

⇒ Remaining work = 48 - 45 = 3

⇒ The remaining work is completed in = 3 / 4 days

⇒ Total days to complete the  work = 13 + 3/4 = 13\(\frac{3}{4}\)

Hence, The total work is completed in 13\(\frac{3}{4}\) days

questions.question: 2 men can finish a work in 6 days and 3 women can finish the same work in 4 days. In how many days will the work be finished by 1 man and 2 women, working together every day?
questions.questionHtml: 2 men can finish a work in 6 days and 3 women can finish the same work in 4 days. In how many days will the work be finished by 1 man and 2 women, working together every day?
questions.solution:
2M × 6 = 3W × 4 ⇒ M/W = 1/1

Total work = 3W × 4 = 3 × 1 × 4 = 12 units 

Time taken to complete the work by 1 man and 2 woman = 12/(1 + 2) = 12/3 = 4 days

questions.question: A can finish a piece of work by working alone in 4 days. B, while working alone, can finish the same work in 12 days. If both of them work together, then in how many days will the work be completed?
questions.questionHtml: A can finish a piece of work by working alone in 4 days. B, while working alone, can finish the same work in 12 days. If both of them work together, then in how many days will the work be completed?
questions.solution:
L.C.M (4,12) = 12 (Total work)

A does = 12/4 = 3 units of work in one day, B does = 12/12 = 1 unit of work in one day.

Together, A and B do 3 + 1 = 4 units of work in one day.

So, they finish work in 12 / 4 = 3 days.

questions.questionHtml: 6 men and 8 women can do a piece of work in 10 days, whereas 26 men and 48 women can do the same work in 2 days. What will be the time taken by 15 men and 20 women to do the same work?

Then,15 men and 20 women can do the same work in

⇒ 200/ (15x2 + 20 x1) ⇒ 200/50 ⇒ 4days

questions.question: P and Q can do a work in 12 days and 9 days, respectively. They both worked together and earned ₹63,000. The share of P (in Rs.) is:
questions.questionHtml: P and Q can do a work in 12 days and 9 days, respectively. They both worked together and earned ₹63,000. The share of P (in Rs.) is:
questions.solution:
Given:

P can complete the work in 12 days.

Q can complete the work in 9 days.

Total earnings for the work = ₹63,000

Formula Used:

Work done by P in one day = 1 / 12

Work done by Q in one day = 1 / 9

Combined work done by P and Q in one day = (1 / 12) + (1 / 9)

Share of P = (Work done by P) / (Total work) × Total earnings

Calculation:

Combined work done by P and Q in one day:

LCM of 12 and 9 = 36

Work done by P in one day = 3 / 36

Work done by Q in one day = 4 / 36

Combined work done in one day = (3 / 36) + (4 / 36) = 7 / 36

Ratio of work done by P and Q:

Ratio = Work done by P : Work done by Q = 3 : 4

Let the total work be divided into 7 parts (3 parts by P and 4 parts by Q).

Share of P = (3 / 7) × 63,000

⇒ Share of P = 27,000

The share of P is ₹27,000

questions.question: A and B together can complete a work in 20 days. B and C together can complete the same work in 15 days. If A, B and C all work together, then the same work gets completed in 10 days. How many days will A and C together take to complete the same work?
questions.questionHtml: A and B together can complete a work in 20 days. B and C together can complete the same work in 15 days. If A, B and C all work together, then the same work gets completed in 10 days. How many days will A and C together take to complete the same work?
questions.solution:
Efficiency of A and B together = 60/20 = 3 .......(i)

Efficiency of B and C together = 60/15 = 4 ........(ii)

Efficiency of A, B and C together = 60/10 = 6.  .......(iii)

Solve (i) and (iii), Efficiency of C = 6 - 3 = 3

Put in (ii), Efficiency of B = 4 - 3 = 1

Put in (i), Efficiency of A = 3 - 1 = 2, Efficiency of A + C = 3 + 2 = 5

A and B together can complete a work = 60/5 = 12 days

∴ 20 men will take 48 days to paint 20 walls.

questions.question: A and B can do a work in 15 days and 10 days respectively. They begin the work together but B leaves after two days. Now A completes the remaining work. The total number of days needed for the completion of the work is:
questions.questionHtml: A and B can do a work in 15 days and 10 days respectively. They begin the work together but B leaves after two days. Now A completes the remaining work. The total number of days needed for the completion of the work is:
questions.solution:
Given:

A can-do work in 15 days

B can do work in 10 days 

Concept used:

A can do a work in n days 

So, A's one day work = 1/n

Calculation: 

A can-do a work in 15 days 

⇒ A's one-day work = 1/15

B can do a work in 10 days

⇒ B's  one day work = 1/10

A and B's one day work = 1/15 + 1/10

⇒ 5/30 = 1/6

Two days work of A and B will be 2/6 = 1/3

Remaining work after B left = 1- 1/3 = 2/3

A will finished remaining work in = (2/3) × 15 =  10 days

∴ Total number of days to complete work is 10 + 2 = 12 days  

Shortcut Trick

LCM of 15 and 10 is 30 

A = 15 × 2 = 30

B = 10 × 3 = 30

Total work = 30 unit

B does 3 unit work in one day

A does 2 unit work in one day

⇒ (A + B)'s one day's work is (3 + 2) unit = 5 unit

⇒ (A + B)'s two days' work is (5 × 2) unit = 10 unit

⇒ Remaining work = 30 - 10 = 20 unit 

A will complete remaining work in, 20/2 = 10 days 

Total number of days = (10 + 2) days = 12 days

∴ Total number of days to complete work is 12 days

questions.question: P and Q can complete a job in 4 days and 12 days, respectively. They work on alternate days with P starting the job. In how many days will the job be completed?
questions.questionHtml: P and Q can complete a job in 4 days and 12 days, respectively. They work on alternate days with P starting the job. In how many days will the job be completed?
questions.solution:
Work done by P in 1 day = 1/4, Work done by Q in 1 day = 1/12

Work done in 2 days = 1/4 + 1/12 = 1/3

Total work = 1, Number of cycles = 1 / (1/3) = 3, Total days = 3 × 2 = 6 days

questions.question: Tina alone can do a piece of work in 12 days and Meena alone can do the same work in 15 days, If Tina and Meena undertook to do this work for Rs. 18,000, then how much amount will Meena get, if they work together?
questions.questionHtml: Tina alone can do a piece of work in 12 days and Meena alone can do the same work in 15 days, If Tina and Meena undertook to do this work for Rs. 18,000, then how much amount will Meena get, if they work together?
questions.solution:
A = 12 × 5 = 60, B = 15 × 4 = 60

A can do 5 unit in one day, B can do 4 unit in one day 

Total days to complete work = 60/9 days  =20/3

questions.question: 4 men and 8 women complete a job in 10 days, and 5 men and 24 women complete the same work in 4 days. In how many days will 1 man and 1 woman complete the same work?
questions.questionHtml: 4 men and 8 women complete a job in 10 days, and 5 men and 24 women complete the same work in 4 days. In how many days will 1 man and 1 woman complete the same work?
questions.solution:
Total work is the same.

So,

⇒ (4M + 8W) × 10 = (5M + 24W) × 4

⇒ 20M = 16W

⇒ 5M = 4W

Now total work will be 14 × 10 = 140 units

1 M +  1W = (1 + 5/4) M

⇒ 9/4 M 

Number of days required 

⇒ 140 × 4 / 9 = \(62 \frac{2}{9}\) days

questions.questionHtml: 40 men can complete a work in 30 days. However, if 10 men leave the group, how many days will the group take to complete the work?

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 66 days and B can do the same work in two-third of the time taken by A. Working together, what part of the same work can they complete in 12 days?
questions.questionHtml: A can do a piece of work in 66 days and B can do the same work in two-third of the time taken by A. Working together, what part of the same work can they complete in 12 days?
questions.solution:
B does half of the work in two-thirds of the time taken by A ⇒ B completes the work in = \(2\over 3\) × 66 = 44 days. LCM of 44 and 66 = 132. Efficiency of A = \(132\over66\) = 2 units /day, Efficiency of B = \(132\over 44\) = 3 units /day.

Total efficiency of A and B = 2 + 3 = 5 units /day, Total work done in 12 days = 5 × 12 = 60 units

Part of the work done = \(60\over132\) = \(\frac{5}{{11}}\) days.

questions.question: 8 men can complete a work in 45 days. 8 women can complete the same work in 18 days. In how many days will 5 men and 8 women, together, complete the same work?
questions.questionHtml: 8 men can complete a work in 45 days. 8 women can complete the same work in 18 days. In how many days will 5 men and 8 women, together, complete the same work?
questions.solution:
Let, M = Man and W = Woman

⇒ 8M × 45 = 8W × 18 ⇒ M/W = 2/5Total work = (8 × 2) × 45 = 720

The total work done by 5 men and 8 women for one day = (5 × 2) + (8 × 5) = 50 

The total time taken by them: ⇒ 720/50 ⇒ 14(2/5)

questions.question: A can complete one-fourth of a work in 2 days and B can complete three-fifth of the same work in 6 days. In how many days will they complete the work if they work together?
questions.questionHtml: A can complete one-fourth of a work in 2 days and B can complete three-fifth of the same work in 6 days. In how many days will they complete the work if they work together?
questions.solution:
Formula:

Efficient = Total work ÷ Time taken to complete work individually

Calculation:

According to the question-

A does one-fourth of the work in 2 days.

⇒ A completes the work in \(2\over{1\over4}\) = 8 days

Similarly, B completes three-fifth of the same work in 6 days

⇒ B completes the work in \(6\over{3\over5}\) = 10 days

LCM of 8 and 10 = 40

Let us assume the total work to be 40 units.

Efficiency of A = \(40\over 8\) = 5 units /day

Efficiency of B = \(40\over 10\) = 4 units /day

Total efficiency of A and B = 5 + 4 = 9 units /day

Total time needed = 40 ÷ 9 = \(40\over9 \)= 4\(4\over9 \) days.

∴ The total time required is 4\(4\over9 \)  days.

questions.question: 20 men can finish a work in 220 days, but at the end of 90 days, 20 additional men are employed. In how many more days will the work be completed?
questions.questionHtml: 20 men can finish a work in 220 days, but at the end of 90 days, 20 additional men are employed. In how many more days will the work be completed?
questions.solution:
20 men can finish a work in 220 days but the first 90 days done remaining days (220 - 90) = 130, then 20 more joined

⇒ 130 × 20 = k × 40 ⇒ k = (130 × 20)/40 = 65 days

Thus, Work will be completed after 65 more days.

questions.question: P alone can complete a piece of work in 10 days while Q alone can complete the same piece of work in 15 days. To complete the work in 4 days, R is hired by P and Q. How many days does R take to complete the work alone?
questions.questionHtml: P alone can complete a piece of work in 10 days while Q alone can complete the same piece of work in 15 days. To complete the work in 4 days, R is hired by P and Q. How many days does R take to complete the work alone?
questions.solution:
Let R alone complete the work in x days.

⇒ 1-day work of R = 1/x ⇒ (1/10) + (1/15) + (1/x) = 1/4 ⇒ (1/6) + (1/x) = 1/4

⇒ 1/x = (1/4) – (1/6) ⇒ 1/x = 1/12 ⇒ x = 12 days

questions.question: Geeta can assemble a toy in 10 minutes, whereas Sudha can assemble the same toy in 15 minutes. If they work together, how much time will they take to assemble 60 toys?
questions.questionHtml: Geeta can assemble a toy in 10 minutes, whereas Sudha can assemble the same toy in 15 minutes. If they work together, how much time will they take to assemble 60 toys?
questions.solution:
Given:

Geeta can assemble a toy in 10 minutes.

Sudha can assemble the same toy in 15 minutes.

Concept used:

Entire work = Work done in each minute × Time taken (in minutes)

Calculation:

LCM (10,15) = 30

Let the entire work (making a toy) be the LCM of the time taken by Geeta & Sudha.

So, the entire work =  30 units

Geeta does in a minute = 30 ÷ 10 = 3 units of work

Sudha does in a minute = 30 ÷ 15 = 2 units of work

Time taken to finish the entire work together = 30 ÷ (3 + 2) = 6 minutes 

So, time taken to make 60 toys together = 6 × 60 = 360 minutes = 6 hours

∴ If they work together, they will take 6 hours to assemble 60 toys.

questions.question: A can complete a task in the same time in which B and C work together. If A and B could complete it jointly in 10 days and C alone in 50 days, then B could complete it independently in:
questions.questionHtml: A can complete a task in the same time in which B and C work together. If A and B could complete it jointly in 10 days and C alone in 50 days, then B could complete it independently in:
questions.solution:
Given:

A complete the work in the same time as B + C work together

A + B can complete a work = 10 days

C can alone complete a work = 50 days

Formula Used:

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

Calculation:

LCM of (10, 50) = 50 units = Total Work

Efficiency of C = 1 unit/day

Efficiency of A + B = 5 unit/day

Let the efficiency of B = y

Efficiency of B + C = Efficiency of A

⇒ y + 1 = A

⇒ y + 1 = 5 - y          (A + B = 5 ⇒ A = 5 - B)

⇒ 2y = 4 

⇒ y = 2

Time taken by B to complete the work = total work/efficiency

⇒ 50 / 2 = 25 days

∴ The time taken by B to complete the work is 25 days.

questions.question: Riya and Sangeeta can finish a work in 6 days and 8 days, respectively. Riya started the work alone and then after 3 days, Sangeeta joined Riya. They both finish the remaining work. How long did the total work last?
questions.questionHtml: Riya and Sangeeta can finish a work in 6 days and 8 days, respectively. Riya started the work alone and then after 3 days, Sangeeta joined Riya. They both finish the remaining work. How long did the total work last?
questions.solution:
Riya's work rate = 1/6, Sangeeta's work rate = 1/8

Work done by Riya in 3 days = 3 × (1/6) = 1/2

Remaining work = 1 - 1/2 = 1/2 ⇒ Combined work rate = 1/6 + 1/8 = (7/24)

Time for remaining work = (1/2)/(7/24) = (12/7) days

Total time = 3 + (12/7) = (33/7) = \(4 \frac{5}{7}\) days

questions.question: 10 women can do a work in 6 days and 6 men can do the same work in 5 days. If all these men and women work together, then how many days will they take to finish this work?
questions.questionHtml: 10 women can do a work in 6 days and 6 men can do the same work in 5 days. If all these men and women work together, then how many days will they take to finish this work?
questions.solution:
Given :

Work Done = time × efficiency

Calculation :

⇒ 60W = 30M

⇒ W/M = 1/2

Total Work = 60

Time = 60/(10 × 1 + 6 × 2)

⇒ 60/22 = 30/11

⇒ \(2 \frac{8}{11}\)

questions.question: A alone can complete the project in 10 days; B alone can complete it in 20 days while C alone can complete it in 30 days. They together earn Rs. 1,100 for the project. By how much do the total earnings of A and C exceed the earnings of B?
questions.questionHtml: A alone can complete the project in 10 days; B alone can complete it in 20 days while C alone can complete it in 30 days. They together earn Rs. 1,100 for the project. By how much do the total earnings of A and C exceed the earnings of B?
questions.solution:
A's work/day : B's work/day : C's work/day = 1/10 : 1/20 : 1/30 = 6 : 3 : 2

Earnings of A and C = (6 + 2)/11 ×  Rs. 1,100 = Rs. 800

Earnings of B = 3/11 × Rs. 1,100 = Rs. 300

Difference = Rs. 800 - Rs. 300 = Rs. 500
